Railo — Security fixes, not security alerts.

Railo is an automated security remediation platform designed for modern engineering teams.

Most security tools stop at vulnerability detection. They generate alerts and dashboards, but developers still need to investigate the issue, write a fix, and verify the change. This process slows development and leaves vulnerabilities unresolved.

Railo changes that.

What Railo does

Railo automatically identifies and fixes common application security vulnerabilities including:

• SQL Injection

• Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)

• Hardcoded secrets

• Command injection

• Path traversal

• Server-side request forgery (SSRF)

Every fix is minimal, transparent, and validated through CI pipelines.



Why Railo exists

Security scanners generate alerts, but developers still have to fix the code.

Railo was built to close the gap between security detection and remediation by automatically generating safe code fixes.

Instead of telling developers what is broken, Railo helps fix it.

Our platform focuses on practical security systems designed for modern digital companies and the evolving regulatory environment in India.

Core components of the platform include:

properties.name: Faramesh Labs
properties.description:
Most agents in production have way more permissions than the job actually needs. They can call any tool, hit any endpoint, move money. You usually find out something went sideways when something goes sideways.

Faramesh sits between your agent and the tools it calls, gating every action through a policy first. Permit, deny, or defer to a human. Credentials, identity, per-tool rules, audit trails, all defined as code in one file. Policies are written in FPL, our DSL with proper handling for sessions, budgets, delegation, and mandatory deny. One file, version controlled, deployed with faramesh apply. Basically Terraform, if Terraform's job was telling your agent no.

The enforcement is deterministic. No LLM watching another LLM hoping it makes the right call. Same policy, same decision, every time. Works with 13 frameworks out of the box including LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and MCP. Most setups need no code changes, you prepend faramesh run and the framework gets patched automatically.

Open source. Free to start.

entity.name: Railo
entity.description:
Railo — Security fixes, not security alerts.

Railo is an automated security remediation platform designed for modern engineering teams.

Most security tools stop at vulnerability detection. They generate alerts and dashboards, but developers still need to investigate the issue, write a fix, and verify the change. This process slows development and leaves vulnerabilities unresolved.

Railo changes that.

Railo analyzes pull requests, detects security vulnerabilities, and automatically generates safe patches. These fixes are submitted as reviewable pull requests that developers can merge just like any other code change.

Railo helps teams turn security remediation into a natural part of the development workflow.



What Railo does

Railo automatically identifies and fixes common application security vulnerabilities including:

• SQL Injection

• Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)

• Hardcoded secrets

• Command injection

• Path traversal

• Server-side request forgery (SSRF)

Every fix is minimal, transparent, and validated through CI pipelines.



Why Railo exists

Security scanners generate alerts, but developers still have to fix the code.

Railo was built to close the gap between security detection and remediation by automatically generating safe code fixes.

Instead of telling developers what is broken, Railo helps fix it.

Our platform focuses on practical security systems designed for modern digital companies and the evolving regulatory environment in India.

Shadow Security aims to strengthen the connection between organizations and the ethical hacking community while helping companies build measurable and provable security practices.

entity.name: Faramesh Labs
entity.description:
Most agents in production have way more permissions than the job actually needs. They can call any tool, hit any endpoint, move money. You usually find out something went sideways when something goes sideways.

Faramesh sits between your agent and the tools it calls, gating every action through a policy first. Permit, deny, or defer to a human. Credentials, identity, per-tool rules, audit trails, all defined as code in one file. Policies are written in FPL, our DSL with proper handling for sessions, budgets, delegation, and mandatory deny. One file, version controlled, deployed with faramesh apply. Basically Terraform, if Terraform's job was telling your agent no.

The enforcement is deterministic. No LLM watching another LLM hoping it makes the right call. Same policy, same decision, every time. Works with 13 frameworks out of the box including LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and MCP. Most setups need no code changes, you prepend faramesh run and the framework gets patched automatically.

Open source. Free to start.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

properties.name: Faramesh Labs

Most agents in production have way more permissions than the job actually needs. They can call any tool, hit any endpoint, move money. You usually find out something went sideways when something goes sideways.

Faramesh sits between your agent and the tools it calls, gating every action through a policy first. Permit, deny, or defer to a human. Credentials, identity, per-tool rules, audit trails, all defined as code in one file. Policies are written in FPL, our DSL with proper handling for sessions, budgets, delegation, and mandatory deny. One file, version controlled, deployed with faramesh apply. Basically Terraform, if Terraform's job was telling your agent no.

The enforcement is deterministic. No LLM watching another LLM hoping it makes the right call. Same policy, same decision, every time. Works with 13 frameworks out of the box including LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and MCP. Most setups need no code changes, you prepend faramesh run and the framework gets patched automatically.

Open source. Free to start.

• Hardcoded secrets

Every fix is minimal, transparent, and validated through CI pipelines.



Why Railo exists

Security scanners generate alerts, but developers still have to fix the code.

Railo was built to close the gap between security detection and remediation by automatically generating safe code fixes.

Instead of telling developers what is broken, Railo helps fix it.

• Open source licence compliance

• Export control

Trusted by global enterprises including Cariad, Ericsson, LG, and Siemens. SOC 2, ISO 27001, and GDPR compliant.
Headquartered in Madrid. Distributed team across multiple regions and time zones.

Our platform focuses on practical security systems designed for modern digital companies and the evolving regulatory environment in India.

Core components of the platform include:

Astra — an on-demand security scanner that detects exposed services, maps CVEs, and identifies security misconfigurations across web assets and infrastructure. Organizations receive a security score and a certificate reflecting their current security posture.

Shadow Security aims to strengthen the connection between organizations and the ethical hacking community while helping companies build measurable and provable security practices.

entity.name: Faramesh Labs
entity.description:
Most agents in production have way more permissions than the job actually needs. They can call any tool, hit any endpoint, move money. You usually find out something went sideways when something goes sideways.

Faramesh sits between your agent and the tools it calls, gating every action through a policy first. Permit, deny, or defer to a human. Credentials, identity, per-tool rules, audit trails, all defined as code in one file. Policies are written in FPL, our DSL with proper handling for sessions, budgets, delegation, and mandatory deny. One file, version controlled, deployed with faramesh apply. Basically Terraform, if Terraform's job was telling your agent no.

The enforcement is deterministic. No LLM watching another LLM hoping it makes the right call. Same policy, same decision, every time. Works with 13 frameworks out of the box including LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and MCP. Most setups need no code changes, you prepend faramesh run and the framework gets patched automatically.

Open source. Free to start.

• Custom software development
• Full-stack web and mobile product development
• AI-powered applications and automation

Our Approach

entity.name: Capsule Security
entity.description:
Every AI Agent Needs a Guardian. We Built It.

AI agents are the most powerful and most ungovernable workforce your organization has ever deployed. They write code, access databases, make API calls, and take autonomous action across your most sensitive systems. They move fast. They don't ask permission. And when they go rogue, no one sees it coming.

Until now.

Capsule Security is the runtime security platform for AI agents. Our Guardian Agent technology monitors every action an AI agent takes in real time and enforces security policies before damage is done. No proxies. No gateways. No SDKs. Just seamless, native integration that gives your security team full visibility and real-time control without slowing anything down.

We don't scan. We don't log after the fact. We enforce.

What makes us different:
→ Patented fine-tuned small language models that understand agent intent, not just tokens
→ Native hooks and API-level integration with leading AI platforms
→ Real-time policy enforcement that stops threats mid-action
→ Full visibility into the complete agent action chain
→ Zero friction for engineering teams. No code changes, no architectural rework
Capsule was named a Representative Vendor in Gartner's inaugural Market Guide for Guardian Agents. Our research team has disclosed zero-day vulnerabilities in AI Agent platforms, because we believe the industry deserves to know what AI agents are actually capable of.

Backed by LAMA Partners and ForgePoint Capital International and advised by leading security leaders.

Your AI agents are already inside your perimeter. The question is: who's watching them?

We are.

entity.description:
safeguard.sh delivers comprehensive software supply chain security through an integrated platform providing complete visibility, intelligent governance, and autonomous remediation across the entire software development lifecycle.
The Challenge
Over 90% of enterprise applications incorporate open-source components, with 95% of vulnerabilities originating from these dependencies. Incidents like SolarWinds, Log4j, and XZ Utils demonstrate traditional tools are insufficient.
Our Solution: The Complete Software Healing Cycle
SBOM 360 Management
Complete software bill of materials intelligence with deep dependency analysis and real-time risk assessment. Achieve transparency across every component while maintaining compliance with Executive Order 14028 and international standards.
Third-Party Risk Management
Advanced TPRM capabilities providing continuous vendor security assessment, automated SBOM validation, and comprehensive supply chain mapping. Proactively identify and mitigate third-party risks before production impact.
Governance, Oversight & Security
Centralized policy enforcement ensuring consistent security standards and regulatory compliance. Support for NIST, ISO 27001, SOC 2, FedRAMP, and industry-specific requirements.
Automated Vulnerability Remediation
AI-powered autonomous resolution that goes beyond detection. Self-healing capabilities automatically fix vulnerabilities across thousands of containers and repositories, reducing remediation time from weeks to minutes.
Measurable Impact
95%+ reduction in critical vulnerability exposure, 80% decrease in remediation time, 60% reduction in security team effort—enabling faster software delivery without compromising security.
Get Started
Headquartered in San Francisco, serving enterprise organizations and government agencies worldwide.
Visit: safeguard.sh
Contact: hi@safeguard.sh

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.

  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.

  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.

  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.

  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.

  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.

  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

• SQL Injection

• Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)

• Hardcoded secrets

• Path traversal

Every fix is minimal, transparent, and validated through CI pipelines.



Why Railo exists

Security scanners generate alerts, but developers still have to fix the code.

Railo was built to close the gap between security detection and remediation by automatically generating safe code fixes.

Instead of telling developers what is broken, Railo helps fix it.

properties.name: Grego AI
properties.description:
Grego AI is an AI-native security research company built by real bounty hunters. People who spent years finding and validating vulnerabilities in production protocols before encoding that workflow into an autonomous system.

Traditional security audits have a hard ceiling. The human mind can only trace so many layers of interacting systems at once. The most critical vulnerabilities, the ones buried across 5, 6, 7 levels of system dependencies, fall outside what any reviewer can hold in their head simultaneously. Not a skill issue. A cognitive constraint. For decades, that constraint defined the outer limit of what security auditing could catch. Grego was built to go past it.

Our system ingests entire codebases, maps every module and dependency, and tests for vulnerabilities at depths that manual review cannot reach. Where traditional audits trace what a human can follow, Grego traces everything. Autonomous sub-agents explore parallel attack paths, findings are validated in live sandboxes, and every result is delivered as a complete, reproducible report.

The protocols we have helped secure include Lido, Chainlink, Aave, Uniswap, Polygon, and Euler. Each of our findings have immediately been cleared by the protocol in question. None of it was caught by a human reviewer first.

Our track record: 50+ confirmed vulnerabilities across live protocols, a top-3 finish out of 429 participants in a public audit competition. 

This is not a smarter scanner or a faster checklist. It is a fundamentally different capability. An entire class of previously invisible vulnerabilities is now detectable for the first time.

Built by researchers with proof, not opinions.

Most transaction risk isn’t created during a sale process - it’s exposed by it.
 
By the time a business goes to market, many of the factors that determine value and deal certainty are already in place. We work with business owners and their advisors to evaluate those factors before the market does.
 
At Cogent Equity, we represent a limited number of companies with $1M to $10M in adjusted EBITDA, typically with long operating histories and strong underlying performance. Our focus is not just on running a process, but on ensuring the business is positioned to succeed in one.
 
This work often begins before a sale is imminent. We evaluate the business the way a sophisticated buyer would - identifying value constraints, aligning expectations, and addressing issues that would otherwise surface during diligence.
 
For advisors, the situations where it tends to be most useful to involve us are:
 
 - An owner is beginning to consider a sale in the next 1–3 years 
 - Valuation expectations are unclear or misaligned 
 - There are known or suspected issues that could impact a transaction 
 
Our perspective is shaped by firsthand experience as owners , operators, buyers, and sellers across nine different industries - allowing me to evaluate businesses the way a sophisticated buyer actually would.
 
While much of our work begins before a sale, we also represent owners through a structured, buyer-focused transaction process when the timing is right.
 
The objective is not just the right deal, but the right buyer - and a process that holds together from start to finish.

entity.name: Eindhoven Career Platform
entity.description:
Finding your dream career in a world full of options and opportunities can be hard. Therefore, a few years ago, the Eindhoven Career Platform (ECP) was brought to life. The platform should be the bridge between companies and Industrial Engineering students. Before the release of ECP, both companies and students had difficulties in finding connections and creating the perfect match between students and opportunities. This makes ECP a great solution for bringing the two together. ECP offers opportunities such as internships, Bachelor End Projects, student jobs, master theses, and starting positions. 

The platform offers a vast range of available industries. Examples are consultancy, supply chain, data science & IT, and manufacturing. All companies can put vacancies on the platform to find the required student for their career opportunity. This ensures that there is always something available for every type of student. Currently, the ECP hosts over 50 different vacancies and thus has proven to be the solution for the difficulty in finding the right opportunity. A platform like ECP requires constant evaluation and innovation. Therefore, the ECP committee takes the platform into its guard. The current committee consists of Julian de Rozario, Bram van der Pluijm, Rogier Zondag, and Jens Adriaanse, the officer of external affairs of the Industria Board.

Through constant evaluation and increasing awareness, the ultimate goal of the platform is to become the platform for career opportunities for all students in Eindhoven. Besides, we are aiming to keep a diversified range of job opportunities, to maximize the chance for students to find a job opportunity to suits their interests bests. So, if you are looking for an interesting job, master thesis, bachelor end project, or a student job? Then have a scroll at ECP. Are you looking for an ambitious Industrial Engineering student? Then do not hesitate and get in contact!

entity.name: Railo
entity.description:
Railo — Security fixes, not security alerts.

Railo is an automated security remediation platform designed for modern engineering teams.

Most security tools stop at vulnerability detection. They generate alerts and dashboards, but developers still need to investigate the issue, write a fix, and verify the change. This process slows development and leaves vulnerabilities unresolved.

Railo changes that.

Railo analyzes pull requests, detects security vulnerabilities, and automatically generates safe patches. These fixes are submitted as reviewable pull requests that developers can merge just like any other code change.

Railo helps teams turn security remediation into a natural part of the development workflow.



What Railo does

Railo automatically identifies and fixes common application security vulnerabilities including:

• SQL Injection

• Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)

• Hardcoded secrets

• Command injection

• Path traversal

• Server-side request forgery (SSRF)

Every fix is minimal, transparent, and validated through CI pipelines.



Why Railo exists

Security scanners generate alerts, but developers still have to fix the code.

Railo was built to close the gap between security detection and remediation by automatically generating safe code fixes.

Instead of telling developers what is broken, Railo helps fix it.

entity.name: Shadow Security
entity.description:
Shadow Security builds security infrastructure that helps organizations identify vulnerabilities, manage responsible disclosure, and strengthen data governance.

Our platform focuses on practical security systems designed for modern digital companies and the evolving regulatory environment in India.

Core components of the platform include:

Shastra — a DPDP data governance runtime that records consent, access, and deletion events to generate verifiable compliance evidence.

Suraksha VDP — a vulnerability disclosure platform that provides organizations with a structured channel to receive, triage, and resolve security vulnerabilities reported by ethical hackers.

Astra — an on-demand security scanner that detects exposed services, maps CVEs, and identifies security misconfigurations across web assets and infrastructure. Organizations receive a security score and a certificate reflecting their current security posture.

Shadow Security aims to strengthen the connection between organizations and the ethical hacking community while helping companies build measurable and provable security practices.

entity.name: SCANOSS
entity.description:
Every modern codebase is a Frankie — stitched together from open source libraries, copied snippets, internal components, and AI-generated code. Each piece accelerates development. Each one also brings blind spots around origin, obligations, and risk.

SCANOSS is the software risk intelligence platform that makes software composition transparent and verifiable at scale.
We help engineering, security, and compliance teams understand what is actually inside their codebases — declared dependencies, undeclared snippets, AI-assisted code, and cryptographic algorithms — so they can build inventories that stand up to audit and make decisions based on evidence.

What sets SCANOSS apart:
— Real-time, developer-first SCA built for modern DevSecOps workflows
— Snippet-level detection that surfaces hidden, copied, and AI-generated code
— Cryptographic detection with full CBOM generation in CycloneDX 1.6, aligned with EU Cyber Resilience Act, NIST SSDF, IEC 62443, and DO-178C
— API-first and modular, designed to integrate with the toolchains you already use
— Open source at the core. Our dataset became the foundation of the SPDX Crypto Algorithm List V1.0

Use cases:
• Open source licence compliance
• AI-assisted code governance
• Post-quantum cryptography readiness
• Vulnerability discovery
• Export control

Trusted by global enterprises including Cariad, Ericsson, LG, and Siemens. SOC 2, ISO 27001, and GDPR compliant.
Headquartered in Madrid. Distributed team across multiple regions and time zones.

→ Explore our resources: scanoss.com/resources

entity.name: Grego AI
entity.description:
Grego AI is an AI-native security research company built by real bounty hunters. People who spent years finding and validating vulnerabilities in production protocols before encoding that workflow into an autonomous system.

Traditional security audits have a hard ceiling. The human mind can only trace so many layers of interacting systems at once. The most critical vulnerabilities, the ones buried across 5, 6, 7 levels of system dependencies, fall outside what any reviewer can hold in their head simultaneously. Not a skill issue. A cognitive constraint. For decades, that constraint defined the outer limit of what security auditing could catch. Grego was built to go past it.

Our system ingests entire codebases, maps every module and dependency, and tests for vulnerabilities at depths that manual review cannot reach. Where traditional audits trace what a human can follow, Grego traces everything. Autonomous sub-agents explore parallel attack paths, findings are validated in live sandboxes, and every result is delivered as a complete, reproducible report.

The protocols we have helped secure include Lido, Chainlink, Aave, Uniswap, Polygon, and Euler. Each of our findings have immediately been cleared by the protocol in question. None of it was caught by a human reviewer first.

Our track record: 50+ confirmed vulnerabilities across live protocols, a top-3 finish out of 429 participants in a public audit competition. 

This is not a smarter scanner or a faster checklist. It is a fundamentally different capability. An entire class of previously invisible vulnerabilities is now detectable for the first time.

Built by researchers with proof, not opinions.

By the time a business goes to market, many of the factors that determine value and deal certainty are already in place. We work with business owners and their advisors to evaluate those factors before the market does.

This work often begins before a sale is imminent. We evaluate the business the way a sophisticated buyer would - identifying value constraints, aligning expectations, and addressing issues that would otherwise surface during diligence.
 
For advisors, the situations where it tends to be most useful to involve us are:
 
 - An owner is beginning to consider a sale in the next 1–3 years 
 - Valuation expectations are unclear or misaligned 
 - There are known or suspected issues that could impact a transaction 
 
Our perspective is shaped by firsthand experience as owners , operators, buyers, and sellers across nine different industries - allowing me to evaluate businesses the way a sophisticated buyer actually would.
 
While much of our work begins before a sale, we also represent owners through a structured, buyer-focused transaction process when the timing is right.
 
The objective is not just the right deal, but the right buyer - and a process that holds together from start to finish.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
